div.div: أُمُّ الرُّبَيْقِ Calamity, or misfortune: (JK, S, K:) whence the prov., جَآءَنَا بِأمِّ الرُّبَيْقِ عَلَى أُرَيْقِ, (TA,) meaning He brought us a great calamity, or misfortune: (K in art. ارق:) As says that the Arabs assert it to have been said by a man who saw the ghool upon a dusky white camel (جَمَل أَوْرَق); (S in that art., and TA;) أُرَيْق being the dim. of أَوْرَق: (K in that art.:) or امّ الربيق is a name of war, or battle: or the viper: (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, TA:) this last signification is held to be correct by Z, because, he says, the viper is short, and when it folds itself it resembles the رِبَق (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
